При пропускании электрического тока вдол: When an electric current flows along the plate, the moving charges experience the Lorentz force due to the normal component of the induction vector {0}. This force causes the trajectories of the particles to shift toward the edges of the plate, creating surface electric charges {1} there. In the steady state, the electric field created by these charges compensates the Lorentz force. Thus, a Hall electromotive force (EMF) arises between the edges of the plate. The magnitude of this EMF (which we will call the output voltage and denote as {2}) is proportional to the current in the plate and the normal component of the magnetic field induction. When the direction of the induction vector changes, the sign of the output voltage changes. The proportionality coefficient depends on the properties of the plate—its material and geometric dimensions. If the current in the plate is kept constant, the output voltage {3} is proportional to the normal component of the magnetic field induction vector.
